Check: Record the exact deployment identity and scope
Evidence to capture: Deployment or job ID; tenant; site; target device or group; package name and version; requested actor; requested time
Common interpretation: An ambiguous target or package makes later evidence impossible to reconcile
Safe next action: Freeze the original record and create a dated evidence copy before changing anything
Escalation trigger: Target tenant, device, or package identity cannot be proven

Check: Capture the original platform result
Evidence to capture: Console state; timestamps and time zone; progress; return code; stdout; stderr; timeout; retries; audit events
Common interpretation: A summary label can hide whether download, execution, detection, or reporting failed
Safe next action: Export the raw result and retain screenshots before retrying
Escalation trigger: Original evidence has expired or been overwritten

Check: Identify and verify the package artifact
Evidence to capture: Source URL or repository; file name; version; size; cryptographic hash; digital signature; publisher; upload time
Common interpretation: A replaced, corrupt, unsigned, or wrong-architecture artifact can fail differently across devices
Safe next action: Compare the deployed artifact with the approved source and expected hash or signature
Escalation trigger: Artifact provenance or integrity cannot be established

Check: Define success, stop, and rollback conditions
Evidence to capture: Expected installed version; detection rule; business validation; timeout; stop condition; rollback; impact owner
Common interpretation: A green job state is not proof that the intended application is usable
Safe next action: Write measurable acceptance and rollback criteria before remediation
Escalation trigger: No authorized rollback or success test exists

Check: Confirm current endpoint identity and check-in
Evidence to capture: Tenant; site; durable device identity; agent ID; last check-in; power and network state
Common interpretation: An offline, stale, duplicated, or mis-enrolled endpoint can leave a valid deployment pending
Safe next action: Resolve identity and connectivity before changing the package
Escalation trigger: Endpoint ownership or durable identity is disputed

Check: Compare the affected cohort
Evidence to capture: Affected and unaffected targets by tenant; site; OS build; architecture; agent version; network; first-failure time
Common interpretation: A shared boundary often identifies a package, policy, network, or environment fault
Safe next action: Narrow the cohort and choose one representative canary
Escalation trigger: Failure spans multiple tenants or a rapidly growing cohort

Check: Prove each delivery state separately
Evidence to capture: Assigned; queued; downloaded; verified; launched; completed; detected; reported timestamps and identifiers
Common interpretation: One platform label may collapse several distinct deployment states
Safe next action: Locate the last confirmed state and troubleshoot only the next transition
Escalation trigger: The platform cannot expose delivery-state evidence

Check: Check scheduling and platform constraints
Evidence to capture: Service health; queue depth; concurrency; approval state; maintenance window; schedule expiry; supersedence; cancellation
Common interpretation: The package may be valid but blocked, expired, replaced, or waiting for capacity
Safe next action: Clear only the verified constraint or reschedule one canary
Escalation trigger: Provider degradation or queue failure is suspected

Check: Confirm operating-system and architecture requirements
Evidence to capture: OS edition and build; x86 x64 or ARM64; free disk; memory; pending restart; locale; required features
Common interpretation: A package can download successfully but be inapplicable to the endpoint
Safe next action: Correct the narrow prerequisite or exclude the inapplicable device with evidence
Escalation trigger: Prerequisite cannot be met without an unsupported OS or hardware change

Check: Check dependency and version state
Evidence to capture: Required runtimes; frameworks; services; prior versions; conflicting products; product code; upgrade path
Common interpretation: Missing dependencies or unsupported upgrade paths commonly surface as generic installer failures
Safe next action: Install or repair only the documented prerequisite on one canary
Escalation trigger: Dependency change affects a shared production service

Check: Confirm execution identity and session context
Evidence to capture: Configured account; privilege; service or user context; profile; working directory; 32-bit or 64-bit host; interactive requirement
Common interpretation: An installer can work manually but fail under SYSTEM, a service, or a non-interactive session
Safe next action: Reproduce with the intended bounded context on one canary
Escalation trigger: Required privilege or interactive access cannot be justified

Check: Test source and destination reachability
Evidence to capture: DNS; proxy; TLS; firewall; repository; CDN; certificate chain; authentication; same-context download test
Common interpretation: The agent may check in while package storage or installer dependencies remain unreachable
Safe next action: Repair the verified route or trust issue without weakening global controls
Escalation trigger: Shared proxy, certificate, firewall, or repository fault is indicated

Check: Capture the exact command line and parameters
Evidence to capture: Installer executable; arguments; quoting; transforms; properties; silent flags; working directory; redacted secrets
Common interpretation: A malformed silent command can launch, wait for input, install the wrong feature, or expose secrets
Safe next action: Compare with vendor documentation and test the exact redacted command on a disposable canary
Escalation trigger: Command requires undocumented or sensitive parameters

Check: Collect the installer log and first failure
Evidence to capture: Native installer log; RMM agent log; Windows Application and System events; first error; correlated timestamp
Common interpretation: The first local failure is usually more diagnostic than the final platform code
Safe next action: Retain the complete log and trace the first failing action before changing anything
Escalation trigger: Logs contain evidence of corruption, security control, or system instability

Check: Interpret the native return code
Evidence to capture: Raw decimal and hexadecimal code; installer family; platform mapping; restart semantics; vendor documentation
Common interpretation: Platforms can remap success, retry, reboot, and failure codes incorrectly
Safe next action: Map the native code using the installer vendor's documentation and preserve both values
Escalation trigger: Code is undocumented or conflicts with observed endpoint state

Check: Check locks, processes, storage, and restart state
Evidence to capture: Running app or installer processes; file locks; Windows Installer activity; free space; temp path; pending restart evidence
Common interpretation: Another installation, open application, low disk, or pending restart can block or defer completion
Safe next action: Resolve only the verified blocker in an approved window and preserve before-and-after evidence
Escalation trigger: Restart or process termination would disrupt users or services

Check: Review security-control evidence
Evidence to capture: App Control or AppLocker events; EDR or antivirus event; signature result; quarantine; policy ID; allow or block decision
Common interpretation: A control can block the installer, child process, script, or payload even when the download succeeds
Safe next action: Use the documented change process for the narrow signed artifact or rule; do not disable protection globally
Escalation trigger: The artifact is unsigned, unexpected, quarantined, or broadly blocked

Check: Validate the detection rule independently
Evidence to capture: Rule type; file path and version; registry value; product code; script output and exit code; execution context
Common interpretation: Installation may succeed while a stale or incorrect detection rule reports failure, or vice versa
Safe next action: Test the rule against known installed and absent states on one canary
Escalation trigger: Detection produces inconsistent results across contexts

Check: Inventory partial installation and rollback state
Evidence to capture: Files; services; registry; product inventory; shortcuts; scheduled tasks; drivers; rollback log; reboot requirements
Common interpretation: A failed run can leave partial state that makes blind retries destructive or non-repeatable
Safe next action: Document partial effects and follow the vendor-supported repair, uninstall, or rollback path
Escalation trigger: Partial state includes drivers, security software, or shared runtime changes

Check: Check whether the process is still doing bounded work
Evidence to capture: Process tree; child process; CPU and I/O trend; log growth; timeout; UI or input wait; network activity
Common interpretation: A long-running install differs from a hung install, detached child process, or prompt waiting invisibly
Safe next action: Observe within a defined timeout and stop condition before intervening
Escalation trigger: Unbounded activity, resource exhaustion, or user-facing prompt is detected

Check: Correct one verified cause and run one canary
Evidence to capture: Approved change; actor; time; package and command version; target; monitoring; stop condition; rollback
Common interpretation: Changing one variable preserves causal evidence and limits blast radius
Safe next action: Deploy to one representative endpoint with full logging and an explicit timeout
Escalation trigger: Canary failure differs from the original failure or affects business function

Check: Verify installed state independently
Evidence to capture: Installed version; product inventory; service or process; file signature; configuration; launch or business-function test
Common interpretation: Platform success alone does not prove the application is installed and usable
Safe next action: Run the predefined detection and functional checks outside the deployment summary
Escalation trigger: Installed state cannot be verified without unsafe production access

Check: Reconcile the complete target cohort
Evidence to capture: Every target categorized as succeeded; failed; pending; offline; inapplicable; excluded; rolled back; unknown; owned exception
Common interpretation: Aggregate percentages can hide abandoned endpoints and partial rollouts
Safe next action: Assign an owner and dated next action to every non-success target
Escalation trigger: Unknown or failed population exceeds the approved rollout threshold

Check: Record root cause and prevention evidence
Evidence to capture: Root cause; corrected package or rule; monitoring change; customer impact; residual risk; owner; review date; closure evidence
Common interpretation: A deployment is not closed until the fix is reproducible and exceptions are owned
Safe next action: Publish the reusable runbook update and retain a sanitized evidence package
Escalation trigger: Root cause remains unproven or recurrence controls are missing
